summary: Verify 174 fetched RH PDFs: vision identity of image-only files, quote fidelity of load-bearing claims, spot checks
logs: Launching 15 verification agents over the fetched corpus

discrepancies: Orientation quirk (not a content problem): the embedded page TIFFs are stored flipped top-to-bottom; a plain image extraction yields upside-down/mirrored pages and they must be flipped (PIL FLIP_TOP_BOTTOM) to read upright. Any future transcription pipeline must apply this transform.
Environment: the Read tool could not render the PDF directly (pdftoppm/poppler not installed on this machine); pages were verified by extracting embedded images via pypdf and vision-reading the PNGs.
verdicts.notes: Legibility rating: GOOD — suitable for full vision transcription. Clean bitonal photocopy-grade scan, no skew, no cut-off margins, uniform density; all four sampled pages fully readable including dense displayed formulas. Risk areas for transcription fidelity: (1) small superscript exponent strings such as p^{-1-v+(1/2)iz} vs p^{-1-vbar+(1/2)iz} — the overbar on v and chi-bar is thin but visible at full resolution; (2) 1-bit dithering slightly thickens Gamma and integral signs but does not obscure them. Recommend transcribing from pypdf-extracted, top-bottom-flipped page images at native 1824x2745 resolution (as done here), optionally cropping formula regions for zoom. Sampled pages: PDF 1 (=117), 2 (=118), 67 (=183, Theorem 12* and S_n(a,b,z) product), 68 (=184, end of proof + references).

Legibility for future vision reads: GOOD. Rendered at 180 dpi via PyMuPDF (fitz) the scan is clean and fully legible — body text, italics, subscripts (pi_0, A_0), primes (pi', chi', n'), and displayed math (e.g. pi boxtimes pi' of GL(nn'), interval (3/4, 1)) all resolve clearly. Ink is slightly light in places (page 30 especially) but nowhere ambiguous. Practical note: the environment lacks pdftoppm/poppler so the Read tool cannot render PDF pages directly; the working path is python3 + PyMuPDF to rasterize pages to PNG in the scratchpad, then Read the PNGs. Issue number is 1995 No. 6, printed pages 279-308.

discrepancies: Claim 3 page range: chapter actually occupies internal PDF pages 312-341 of p3-25b, not 302-331; the claimed numbers match the printed book page numbers (302-331 region, e.g. internal 313 = printed 303), a uniform +10 internal offset.

Minor transcription artifact in the volume's re-typeset text layer: equation (2) on internal page 313 extracts as "y^2/|mz+n|^{2s}" where the original 1981 scan clearly prints y^s in the numerator. Prose and all other checked formulas are faithful.
verdicts.notes: Both files are genuine and match their labels; the Zagier scan (27 pp, image-only, original 1981 typesetting with the Bonn SFB footnote) and the TIFR volume chapter are the same paper, the volume being a clean LaTeX re-typesetting. Vision reading was done via Read on PNGs rasterized with macOS sips (pdftoppm unavailable; no OCR tools used). Two notes: (1) the chapter's internal PDF range is 312-341, not 302-331 — the claim quoted printed page numbers (offset +10); cite internal 312-341 when extracting from the volume. (2) The volume's text layer has at least one math typo (y^2 for y^s in eq. (2)), so for formula-critical passages prefer cross-checking against the p3-25a scan. Chapter is followed at internal 342 by Zagier's \"Eisenstein Series and the Selberg Trace Formula I\" (printed pp. 303-355 per its bibliography cross-reference).

verdicts.notes: Type-3 bitmap font PDF; text layer unusable as stated, so all verification was by vision on rendered pages 1 and 8-10 (poppler installed to enable the Read tool's page rendering; no OCR tools used, no file modified). 10-page arXiv:math/9812166v1 (3 Dec 1998), "A note on some positivity conditions related to zeta and L-functions", J. B. Conrey and Xian-Jin Li (author order as claimed). Clean text layer; all 12 claims verified via pypdf extraction, no vision fallback needed. All numerical constants match digit-for-digit (5.389100507182945e-69; 111.0295355431696745; 0.000131957; 2.310349004993483456e-45; 0.000422340607; 8714.2). Minor non-discrepancy notes: claim 2 quotes only the if-then core of Theorem 1, which additionally carries four hypotheses on E (accurately signaled by "states: if..."); claim 9's "spreading the failure" is a fair paraphrase, not a quote — the substance (density argument, s0 with Re s0 > 1/2, Re{W(z0)/W(z0+i)} < 0) is verbatim-supported. The two chi_4 witnesses on p.8 lack even equation numbers ((3.2)/(3.4) tag only the zeta witnesses), further supporting claim 11. Paper contains a MATHEMATICA appendix (pp.9-10) reproducing all four computations.

discrepancies: Claim 1: the JFA 281 (2021) 109116 journal citation does not appear anywhere in the y-12 file (it is the arXiv v3 dated 1 Oct 2020); the journal identification is external knowledge, unverifiable from the file.

Claim 5: Section 7.2 is on pp.19-20, not ~p.18, and is titled 'Transform to differential operators'; it treats E(z) = xi_L(s) + xi'_L(s) as the 'genuine Polya-Hilbert space' limit of the perturbation family. The literal phrase 'conjectural Hamiltonian H_L corresponding to E(z) = xi_L(s) + xi'_L(s)' is in Section 8, remark (3), p.21.

Claim 2 (minor): the Hamiltonian (2.10) is defined in the text immediately after Theorem 2.1 ('By Theorem 2.1, the Hamiltonian ... is defined'), not inside the theorem statement itself; Thm 2.1's statement is the existence of tau with det(1 +- K[t]) nonvanishing on [0,tau).
Claim 6 (trivial): the file's sentence ends 'for a finite range of t in R' — the claim's quote stops at 't'.
verdicts.notes: Both PDFs have clean pypdf text layers (y-12: 23 pages; p1-05b: 31 pages); all verification done via text extraction, no OCR needed. All 9 claims confirmed in substance, with four minor discrepancies (see list): the JFA journal reference is absent from the arXiv file, Section 7.2's location/framing is slightly off in the claim (the 'conjectural Hamiltonian H_L' phrase lives in Section 8 remark (3)), the diag/squared-ratio Hamiltonian (2.10) is defined just after Thm 2.1 rather than within it, and one quote omits a trailing 'in R'. Both verbatim quotes (claims 3 and 6, including the as-printed broken English 'to understand it differ from') match the file exactly. Superscripts omega,nu and subscript L in K^{omega,nu}_L, q^{omega,nu}_L(n), gamma^{omega,nu}_L all match the claimed transcriptions.

LOCAL UNIQUENESS ABSENT. No Borg-Marchenko-type or germ-level theorem; \"Borg\", \"Marchenko\", \"germ\" never appear. Uniqueness enters only: (1) globally via Theorem dB — H unique under tr H(t)=1, from [7, Theorem 40]; (2) Theorem 1.2, a global identification (needs E in HB and tau = infinity in (K5), limit t -> infinity) showing the constructed H coincides with the Theorem-dB one — nothing claimed for a finite window [0,t); (3) uniqueness of solutions of the Fredholm equations (Lemmas 2.3/2.4) and of reproducing kernels — analytic tools, not inverse-uniqueness statements. Full theorem list checked: dB, 1.1, 1.2, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, Props 2.1-2.4, Cors 2.1, 5.1 — none local. Bibliography: NO Langer-Woracek, NO Kaltenbaeck-Woracek; DOES cite Romanov-Woracek [24] (discrete spectrum — direct problem) and de Branges [2]-[7]. Fetch decision: germ-level uniqueness must come from outside this paper (e.g. Langer-Woracek local Borg-Marchenko literature), so that fetch remains justified.

refuted.claim: Paper contains a local uniqueness / Borg-Marchenko-type theorem (germ of H on [0,t) determined by/determining partial data).
refuted.evidence: "Borg", "Marchenko", "germ" occur zero times. All "unique(ness)" hits are: (a) solutions of integral equations (Lemmas 2.3, 2.4); (b) reproducing kernels of de Branges subspaces (Sec. 4); (c) global: "H in Theorem dB is unique under the normalization" tr H(t)=1, via [7, Theorem 40]. Theorem 1.2's identification with the de Branges Hamiltonian is global (needs τ=∞ and limit t→∞). No theorem localizes to a finite interval.

Claim 3: w-08 Theorem 1 uses non-strict ≤ in BOTH cases: 'N∗(T) ≤ (1.3208 + o(1))N(T)' under RH — not the claimed strict '<'. Constants 1.3208 / 1.3155 are correct.

Claim 5 parenthetical '(not GRH)' misidentifies the removed hypothesis: w-11 removes GLH (Generalised Lindelöf Hypothesis) from CGG, not GRH; and the paper states 'at least 19/27' (κ∗ ≥ 19/27), phrased as a fraction, not 'more than 70.37%'.

verdicts.notes: All three PDFs are the right papers with the right page counts (16/10/26) and all numerical constants in the claims are correct. MISMATCH is driven by transcription fidelity: every inequality in w-08's Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 is NON-STRICT (≤ / ≥) — the claimed strict '>' (Cor. 2 RH) and '<' (Thm. 1 RH) are wrong — verified both by pypdf text and visually on page 3. The chain of results is internally consistent across the corpus: CGG 1998 prove C_s ⩾ 19/27 under RH+GLH (a referee-added hypothesis per their Remark); Bui-Heath-Brown 2013 remove GLH, getting κ∗ ≥ 19/27 under RH alone; Chirre-Gonçalves-de Laat get 0.6792 (RH) / 0.6845 (GRH) via SDP and explicitly acknowledge 19/27 = 70.37...% as 'currently the best'. w-08 and w-11 are arXiv preprints, so their claimed journal imprints (Adv. Math. 361:106926; Bull. LMS 45:953-961) are unverifiable in-file; w-10 is the published PLMS version with imprint on p. 497.
